Vladislav Tretiak is a Soviet goaltender widely regarded as one of the greatest net minders of all time. His dominance during the Cold War era, including a legendary performance in the nineteen eighty Miracle on Ice Olympics, made him an international icon and proof of Soviet hockey excellence.

He won three Olympic gold medals with the Soviet Union in nineteen seventy-two, nineteen seventy-six, and nineteen eighty-eight, establishing himself as the premier goaltender of the Cold War hockey era. In the nineteen eighty Winter Olympics, Tretiak posted a zero goals-against average when the United States defeated the Soviets in one of hockey's greatest upsets. Despite the loss, Tretiak's performance was extraordinary. He won the World Championship gold medal ten times with the Soviet Union, dominating international competition throughout the nineteen seventies and nineteen eighties.

Tretiak played exclusively in the Soviet league with CSKA Moscow due to Cold War restrictions on player movement, despite being capable of competing in the NHL. He was known for his acrobatic style, quick reflexes, and butterfly-influenced goaltending technique that presaged modern style. He wore number twenty and became a symbol of Soviet hockey prowess during a period of intense geopolitical rivalry. Finally allowed to sign in the NHL at age thirty-nine in nineteen eighty-nine with the Chicago Blackhawks, though his stay was brief, Tretiak remained the only Soviet-trained goaltender to play at the highest American level for decades.
